title: Second Hellenic Republic
capsule: The Second Hellenic Republic was proclaimed by the Greek parliament on 25 March 1924 following King George II's departure and a subsequent plebiscite confirming the republic. Eleftherios Venizelos dominated its politics, serving as prime minister for much of 1928–1933 and securing notable diplomatic gains including normalized Greek-Turkish relations (1930) and the Balkan Pact (1934), while economic crisis led to Greece defaulting on its foreign debts in 1932. General Theodoros Pangalos interrupted constitutional rule with a brief dictatorship in 1925–1926, and the republic was ultimately abolished by a rigged plebiscite on 3 November 1935 that restored the monarchy, paving the way for Ioannis Metaxas's fascist-style 4th of August regime in 1936.
